summary: Linguist Carl Johan Sverdrup Marstrander studied at the University of Oslo (1903–1907) under Sophus Bugge and Alf Torp. He served as Professor of Celtic and comparative linguistics at the School of Irish Learning (1909–1913) and Professor of Celtic philology at Oslo (1913–1953).

Carl Maria Franz Lorinser worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied Catholic theology at the University of Breslau (1839–1841) and continued his studies at the Sapienza University of Rome (1842–1844) and the University of Munich (~1842–1844, Dr. Theol.).

Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig (1834–1838, Doktor der Philosophie ~1834–1842) under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Berlin (~1838–1841). At the University of Oslo, he was a Lektor (1847) and held a Professorenstelle (1857).
Indologist Carl Rabe studied at the University of Breslau (~1841–1845), earning a Ph.D. under the doctoral supervision of Adolf Friedrich Stenzler.

Carl Salemann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1867–1875), where he worked as Librarian (1879–1890) and taught (~1876–1916). He also became Director of the Asiatic Museum in 1890.
Carl Schuster was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University (~1927–1930) and the University of Vienna (~1930–1934).

Carl Schütz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg (1823–1827), under Franz Bopp (~1827–1830), and earned an honorary Ph.D. at Jena (-1831). He taught modern languages at Ratsgymnasium Bielefeld as Oberlehrer from 1834 to 1858.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, also studying under Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried was a scholar of religion, Indology, and linguistics who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Bonn under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, and others. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin and Professor for Old Testament at Jena (1875–1901).
Carl Suneson worked in Indology, studying at Stockholm University (1960–1966) under Siegfried Lienhard and V. Raghavan. In 1966, he became a Docent (Lecturer) at Stockholm University.

Carl Theodor Johannsen worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Kiel (~1823–1826) and Bonn (~1826–1828, Ph.D.), he taught as a Docent at Bonn (1830–1831) and held an extraordinary professorship in Oriental philology at the University of Copenhagen (1833).

Carl W. Ernst, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at Stanford (A.B. 1968–1973) and Harvard (Ph.D. 1975–1981). He was a professor at Pomona College (1981–1992) and Kenan Distinguished Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied in Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin (Promotion 1899–1901). He held professorships in Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carl William Belser was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Michigan (B.A.) and Leipzig (Ph.D. under Friedrich Delitzsch). He served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at Michigan (1891) and Head of the Latin Department at Colorado Boulder (1893).

Historian and Indologist Carl von Noorden studied at Marburg, Bonn (Ph.D.), Berlin, and Paris under Martin Haug and Leopold von Ranke. He was Professor of History at Greifswald, Marburg, Tübingen, Bonn, and Leipzig between 1868 and 1877.

Carl-Martin Edsman was a religious studies scholar who studied at Uppsala University (~1930–1940), Lund University, and the University of Paris (~1937–1938). He held academic posts at Lund University (~1940–1950) and Uppsala University (~1950–1977).

Carlo Bernheimer, who worked in Indology and other fields, studied at the University of Bologna (~1900–1904) under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè. He subsequently served as Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Bologna (1906–1938, and 1945).
Indologist Carlo Della Casa studied at the University of Turin (~1945–1949) under Mario Vallauri. He later held an academic post at the University of Palermo (~1968–1970).

Indologist Carlo Formichi studied in Naples under Michele Kerbaker, Vienna under Georg Bühler, and Kiel under Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held professorships of Sanskrit at Pisa (1898–1899, 1902, 1905) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).
